# Python — names refer to objects

A Python variable is a name bound to an object. Several names can refer to the same mutable object, which is different from Rust's move and borrow rules.

## 1. Aliasing of a mutable list

~~~python
a = [1, 2]
b = a
b.append(3)
print(a)  # [1, 2, 3]
~~~

Both a and b refer to the same list. A shallow copy creates a new outer list but may still share nested objects.

## 2. Mutable defaults are evaluated once

~~~python
def add(x, items=None):
    if items is None:
        items = []
    items.append(x)
    return items

print(add(1)) # [1]
print(add(2)) # [2]
~~~

Using a default list directly can accidentally retain state from earlier calls. The None sentinel creates a fresh list only when needed.

## 3. Generators yield on demand

~~~python
def numbers():
    yield 2
    yield 3

print(sum(numbers())) # 5
~~~

The function pauses at yield and continues when the consumer requests the next item. It does not need to build an entire list first.

## 4. Decorators transform a function binding

~~~python
def loud(fn):
    def wrapper():
        return fn().upper()
    return wrapper

@loud
def greet():
    return "hello"

print(greet()) # HELLO
~~~

Unlike Rust procedural macros, this ordinary Python decorator is applied during execution of the function definition, commonly at import time.

## 5. Type hints and runtime are separate

~~~python
def double(n: int) -> int:
    return n * 2

print(double(3)) # 6
~~~

The annotation communicates intended types to tools; Python does not use it automatically to reject every mismatched runtime argument.

## 6. Await with an event loop

~~~python
import asyncio
async def answer():
    return 42
print(asyncio.run(answer())) # 42
~~~

Asynchronous functions coordinate waiting, not automatic parallel CPU computation. Interpreter and build details matter for threaded execution.

**Sources:** [Python Tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/), [Language Reference](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/), [asyncio](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio.html).
